title: Global Traveler Profile
description: Global Traveler Profile Schema 1.0.0 (first public edition, 19 November 2026). Merges the Travlr ID traveller profile schema v1.1.0 with the preference, accessibility and substance exposure fields of the 17 November 2026 Focus Areas working draft.
$comment: Design rules. (1) One strength scale, $defs/Strength, the HATPro -100 to 100 integer, for every preference and requirement. (2) Each value property carries x-key, the canonical dotted key to use as the graph DataNode key and as consent scope; x-classification, one of public, private, sensitive, specialCategory; and x-kind, one of preference, requirement, fact, tripDefault. x-legacyKeys lists the v1 or graph v2.0 keys it supersedes. x-status strawman marks first-draft fields that still need review by people with clinical or lived expertise. (3) Graph mapping follows x-graphMapping and the field-level x-comparison annotations. (4) Measurements are metric. (5) Identifiers carried from v1.1.0 keep their original spelling.

defaultLanguage.description: ISO 639 language code with optional ISO 3166-1 region

items.description: ISO 639 language code with optional ISO 3166-1 region

consentSettings.description: Consent held by the traveller. A value classified sensitive or specialCategory may be disclosed only to a grantee holding an unexpired, unrevoked grant whose scope covers its x-key. JSON Schema cannot enforce this; the disclosing system must. Evaluate each operation against a single valid grant matching grantee, action, purpose, any restricted context and exact key or whole dotted-segment prefix. Use grantedAt inclusively and expiry or revocation exclusively. For delegates verify current authority for the traveller and operation. Deny on missing or unverifiable authority. General consent flags cannot widen a grant. Project only the fulfilment fields requested and strip internal metadata.

Strength.description: The HATPro preference scale, an integer from -100 to 100, used for every preference and requirement. Reading assumed here and to be confirmed against the HATPro definition: 100 is required, -100 must be avoided, 0 is no preference, and values between are soft preferences of increasing strength. It replaces the v1 priority integer, required flag, supplier rating and constraint severity.

x-graphMapping.factsAndDefaults: Preserve fact and tripDefault values as such, independently of strength.
x-graphMapping.requirementsAndPreferences: For measured limits use the supplied strength, or +100 when omitted. For other unscored requirements retain the requirement as mandatory. For unscored preferences retain the preference. At +100 the condition must hold. At -100 the condition must be avoided. Intermediate scores are soft preferences and zero is neutral. Preserve signed strength, original value, unit and bound, including whether optional fields were omitted. Interpret strength at the individual scored value or array item.
x-graphMapping.comparison: Compare the supplier measurement to the traveller value using x-comparison. Inclusive minimum is gte, inclusive maximum is lte and equality is eq. Preserve the declared unit when the instance omits unit.
